entry.summary: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.
entry.max_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area
entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Iceland's currency is the Icelandic Kroner (ISK). Declare cash of over 10,000 euros or equivalent if you're travelling between Iceland and any non-EU country. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. You'll have to pay a fine on entry or exit if you: don't declare your money give incorrect information You can use major credit cards in most places.

consular.notes: Australia doesn't have an embassy or consulate in Iceland. You can seek consular help from the Canadian Embassy in Reykjavik.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences, even for possession of small amounts of recreational drugs or some prescription medications, include: heavy fines imprisonment being removed from the Schengen area a potential entry ban If you intend to take medication, confirm it's legal in your destination. Check if any rules or restrictions apply. Depending on your medication, you may need to apply for a permit to bring it to your destination. Always carry a copy of your prescription and transport your medication in its original container.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Always carry an ID, such as your driver's licence or a copy of your passport. Penalties for drink driving and speeding are severe and include the following: heavy fines jail sentences Even minor offences can attract fines and jail sentences. If you're found guilty of an offence: you may face jail or deportation you may be banned from the Schengen area
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Australian driving licences are valid in Iceland if you have had your licence for a minimum of 1 year. However, some car rental companies require customers to present an International Driving Permit (IDP) if holding a licence issued outside Europe or North America. Digital driver's licences may not be accepted. If you need an IDP, get this before you leave Australia. An IDP doesn't replace the requirement for a regular driver's license. tourism.detail: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.

meetings.detail: Business meetings are covered, without being employed in the country.

conference.detail: Business travel, including conferences, is covered.

unpaid-speaking.detail: Unpaid speaking during a business visit is generally covered; the paid-activity exclusion is read narrowly.
unpaid-speaking.next: If unsure, ask Embassy of Iceland.

paid-speaking.detail: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Embassy of Iceland.
paid-speaking.next: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Embassy of Iceland.

remote-work.detail: Remote work for an employer outside the EU isn't addressed in the EU guidance read.

entrepreneur.detail: Exploring and meeting fit a business visit; running a business needs national permission.

trade.detail: Business visits are covered; selling or delivering services may be paid activity.
trade.next: Keep the trip to meetings and negotiation.

artist.detail: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Embassy of Iceland.
artist.next: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Embassy of Iceland.

mixed-mission.detail: The visa-free stay covers the business and tourism parts; any paid part needs national permission.

filming.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (journalistic or media purposes)
filming.detail: Journalistic or media purposes are listed among visa-free purposes; paid production work and location permits are national matters.
filming.next: Ask the Embassy of Iceland about filming, and the local authority about locations.

research.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (short-term study or training)
research.detail: Short-term study and training are covered; paid research at an institution is paid activity.
research.next: Ask the Embassy of Iceland if the host pays you.

volunteering.detail: Volunteering isn't addressed in the EU guidance read.
